items.caption:
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy says AI will mean fewer humans doing what they do today.

He says there won't be no people, and that new jobs will arise, some we can't name yet. But he expects much smaller teams of people who work cross-functionally, because the models can get them 80% of the way on many functions.

Would you rather work on a team of 5 or a team of 50?

Source: a16z, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy on Reinventing Amazon for the AI Era. Full video: youtube.com/watch?v=-YMMRQ1qscI

items.caption:
Jensen Huang says coding is going to get automated away.

The NVIDIA CEO compares it to long division: the simple stuff gets automated. But he says the hard problems, in physics, chemistry, biology, computer science and systems thinking, will never go away.

If you were 18 today, what would you study?

Source: Y Combinator, Jensen Huang: The Mindset That Built NVIDIA. Full video: youtube.com/watch?v=I4B37S1dyQQ

items.caption:
Andy Jassy's AI advice to young people, and to his own kids: you can't run away from it.

The Amazon CEO says to learn it, use it a lot and try things outside your comfort zone. Neither of his kids were developers, but they have used AI to build applications. He adds that it doesn't replace critical reasoning and thinking.

What is the first thing you would build with AI?

items.caption:
Jensen Huang says he was scared to go raise money when he started NVIDIA.

He bought a 500-page book on how to start a company and didn't read it, figuring he'd be out of business by the time he finished. He felt he couldn't answer investors' questions, and says he barely can today. His lesson: none of that matters, and this is the greatest time in the last 60 years to start a company.

What is stopping you from starting?

Source: Y Combinator, Jensen Huang: The Mindset That Built NVIDIA. Full video: youtube.com/watch?v=I4B37S1dyQQ

items.caption:
Andy Jassy predicts big companies will have to rewrite almost all of their code for AI agents.

The Amazon CEO says most startups today begin agent native. Some larger companies will figure out how to build at that pace, but the ones that move slowly will be more vulnerable to startups, in his opinion.

Do you think big companies can move fast enough?
